newsitem.title: USA: Grace sees 1997 sales up, spending down.
newsitem.headline: Grace sees 1997 sales up, spending down.

text.p: W.R. Grace & Co Chairman Albert Costello said he expects the company's sales to be up six to sevenpercent over the comparable figure of $3.25 billion in 1996.
He also told the company' annual meeting he expected Grace's 1997 capital spending to be $150 million less than in 1996. In 1996, capital expenditures were $456.6 million.

"We expect sales to grow in 1997 by six to seven percent as compared with last year," he told the annual meeting. For 1996, Grace posted sales and revenues of $3.25 billion, excluding sales and revenues from divested businesses, a company spokeswoman said.

Costello also told the meeting he expected the company's packaging division, with products including plastic films used to package food and non-food products, to have $3 billion in sales by the year 2000, with growth coming half from expansion and half from new products and the sector benefiting from the growth of the Latin American and Asia Pacific middle class.

He said he expected the Davison specialty chemicals products division to have sales of about $1 billion annually by 2000 and its construction products unit, its third core business, to reach about $600 million in annual sales by 2000.

He said demand for Davison's products would come from changes in the refining industry, changing environmental requirements and new product applications for silica products. And he said Grace construction would benefit from infrastructure development in Latin America and Asia, as well as continue to make small, immediately accretive acquisitions.
